c.tagline: Adventure capital of the Chilean Lake District, in the shadow of an active volcano

card: Widely accepted at hotels, tour operators, and mid-range restaurants; small cafés, artisan stalls, colectivos, and rural termas are often cash-only, so carry CLP

taxi.color: Black with a yellow roof-mounted sign ("TAXI")
taxi.fareNote: Meters are inconsistent in Pucón; agree on a fixed price before longer trips (e.g., to Caburgua or the volcano base) since many rides are negotiated flat fares

emergency.note: Fire: 132. There's a small public hospital (Hospital de Pucón) and a Carabineros station on Av. O'Higgins; a seasonal Volcano/Mountain Rescue (CONAF/GOPE) team monitors Villarrica ascents

walk: The town center is compact and very walkable — most restaurants, shops, and the lakefront cluster within a 10-15 minute walk along Av. O'Higgins — but the volcano, national parks, waterfalls, and hot springs are all outside town and require a rental car, tour van, or taxi/colectivo

safety.safety: Very safe — regularly rated one of the safest and most solo-traveler-friendly towns in Chile
safety.crime: Petty theft (unattended bags on the beach, valuables left in parked rental cars) is the main risk; violent crime against tourists is rare. Bigger real risks are outdoor/adventure hazards — volcanic activity, sudden weather changes, and river currents

hood_landmark.La Poza: Playa Grande & the Río Claro–Lago Villarrica confluence
hood_landmark.Camino a Villarrica: Hotel Antumalal & the lakeshore road toward Villarrica
hood_landmark.Villa Las Peñas: Residential hillside streets near the Fresia hostel row

avoid.reason: Car break-ins at trailhead parking lots and belongings left on the lake beach are the main petty-theft risks.

hood_desc: The compact core of town, packed onto and around Av. O'Higgins — outdoor outfitters, currency exchanges, restaurants, artisan markets, and the church-lined plaza. Base for most visitors.
The lakefront district where the Río Claro meets Lago Villarrica; home to Playa Grande beach, boat launches, and views of the volcano across the water. A short walk from the center.
A quieter lakeside residential pocket east of town toward Caburgua, known for eco-lodges, cabañas, and lake access away from the crowds.
The scenic road linking Pucón and Villarrica along the lakeshore, dotted with boutique and design-forward hotels tucked into the araucaria forest.
A hillside residential neighborhood a few blocks back from O'Higgins, popular with backpackers for its cluster of hostels and cheaper cabañas, with volcano views from the upper streets.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink in town.

transit.sys: No formal municipal public transit; local colectivos (shared taxis) and infrequent regional buses link Pucón to Villarrica, Caburgua, and outlying trailheads
transit.hours: Colectivos and rural buses generally run roughly 7am-9pm, thinner service on weekends and in winter shoulder season
transit.pay: Cash (CLP) paid directly to the driver; no transit card
transit.map: No official route map — ask your hotel or the tourist info kiosk on the plaza for current colectivo stops
transit.note: Nearly everyone walks the town center and uses tour vans, rental cars, or taxis/rideshare apps for the volcano, parks, and hot springs

transport.air: Fly into Temuco's La Araucanía International Airport (ZCO), about 100 km / 1-1.5 hr away, with daily domestic flights from Santiago (LATAM, Sky, JetSmart); Pucón's own small airport (ZPC) has only very limited seasonal flights
transport.train: No passenger rail serves Pucón or the surrounding Araucanía region
transport.bus: Frequent long-distance buses (Turbus, Pullman, JAC) connect Pucón to Temuco, Santiago (9-10 hrs), and Valdivia via the main bus terminal on Av. O'Higgins/Palguín
transport.ferry: No ferry service — Lago Villarrica is used for recreational and tour boats only, not scheduled transport
transport.car: Renting a car in Temuco or Pucón is the easiest way to reach Huerquehue, Caburgua, and the termas independently; roads are paved to major sights but can be gravel/unpaved further out

airport.name: La Araucanía International Airport (Temuco)
airport.transport: Regular shuttle/bus transfers and regional buses run between Temuco airport/bus terminal and Pucón; rental cars available at Temuco airport; pre-booked taxi transfers run roughly $60-90 USD

net.m: Entel, Movistar, Claro, and WOM all have coverage in Pucón town; signal can drop in national parks and near the volcano
net.w: Wifi is standard in hotels, hostels, and most cafés/restaurants in the center
net.gb: $8-15 for a prepaid tourist SIM with several GB of data
net.fwn: Standard open internet access; wifi widely available in hotels and cafes
net.ap: eSIMs from Holafly or Airalo work well and can be activated before arrival

tip.s: Tipping guides, drivers, and tour operators ~10% is customary and appreciated but not obligatory
tip.r: Restaurants often add a voluntary 10% service charge to the bill automatically; you can ask to remove it, and it's polite to leave it or round up for good service
